data.name: Prisciano
data.long_meaning: From the Latin priscus, meaning 'ancient, elder.' In Christian tradition, this name was given to those who had shown great wisdom and dedication to their faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name rooted in the wisdom of the past, symbolizing a deep connection to tradition and the teachings of the past.

in_hebrew.name: פרישיאנו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'pashar' (to press, to squeeze, to obtain by pressing), this name means 'God's prize, precious', and was used in the New Testament for Priscilla, a Roman Christian woman who, along with Aquila, ministered to the early Christian community in Corinth and Ephesus.

in_greek.name: Πρισκιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek 'priscos' (ancient, old, priest), this name means 'priest, priestly'. In the New Testament, it is the name of a Roman Christian man who, along with his wife Priscilla, ministered to the early Christian community in Corinth and Ephesus.

in_latin.name: Priscianus
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin 'Priscianus' (priest, ancient, old), this name means 'priest, ancient, old'.

in_english.name: Priscian
in_english.long_meaning: From the Latin 'Priscianus' (priest, ancient, old), this name means 'priest, ancient, old'.

It may serve as a reminder to the bearer to seek knowledge and understanding of the faith and to live a life rooted in the wisdom and teachings of Jesus Christ. Thus, the name Prisciano embodies both personal and communal aspects of spiritual growth and development.
